I’ve been trying to resolve an issue with my Expatrio blocked account and have been very frustrated by the customer support experience.

I need to make some changes to an existing blocked account, and I completed the requested verification steps and provided the information needed to update my blocked account, including the monthly payout amount for the remaining five months. Despite this, I still have not been able to get the issue properly resolved or receive a clear explanation of the appropriate next steps.

What makes this especially frustrating is that blocked accounts are closely tied to visa and residence requirements in Germany, where timing can matter a great deal. When customers are dealing with time-sensitive immigration matters, there needs to be a reliable way to get account issues reviewed and resolved promptly.

I’m posting this review in the hope that someone at Expatrio can look into my case and actually resolve it. I’m happy to update the review once the issue is fixed.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience.

I opened a blocked account with Expatrio and transferred my money as required. However, I have been unable to access my own funds because of a verification issue caused by the way Expatrio handles my name.

To my first name they added my patronymic (father's name). During the POSTIDENT identification process, Deutsche Post correctly identifies me, because their system automatically reads only the first name and surname from my passport. Expatrio, however, insists that my patronymic must be included in my first name, making the verification impossible.

I have exchanged numerous emails with customer support over several weeks, but the issue remains unresolved. Because of this, I cannot access my own money, which has caused serious financial difficulties.

I hope someone from Expatrio's management or complaints department sees this review and contacts me with a practical solution. I would much prefer to resolve this matter directly than escalate it further.

I rarely leave negative reviews, but unfortunately my recent experience with Expatrio has been extremely disappointing.

Opening and funding the blocked account was straightforward, but the process of accessing my own funds afterwards has been unnecessarily stressful and bureaucratic.

I have already fulfilled the purpose for which the blocked account was opened, obtained the official release confirmation (Sperrfreigabe) from the German immigration authorities, and submitted every document requested. Despite this, the process remains stuck in a lengthy review stage with little communication beyond automated responses.

What has been particularly frustrating is that these are my personal savings, which I urgently need for my relocation and accommodation costs. Being told that a simple blocked account closure may take up to four weeks after all required documents have been provided places customers in an extremely difficult position.

I understand that compliance procedures are necessary, but there should be a more efficient process for cases where all legal requirements have already been satisfied.

I sincerely hope Expatrio reviews its blocked account closure procedures, as the current process creates unnecessary financial hardship for customers during what is already a stressful relocation period.

Complaint 1: The Blocked Amount provided by Expatrio does not comply with the official requirements for the German intensive language course residence permit. The actual legal requirement for 12 months is €13,094 (€1,091.17/month), as confirmed by the Munich Foreigners Office. 

Expatrio only allowed me to deposit €12,133. After transfer fees, the confirmation they issued showed just €11,904 (€992/month), which is below the legal threshold. You can verify this on their own calculator Expatrio's website. 

As a result, the Foreigners Office contacted me, stating the amount was insufficient and requested an additional deposit along with a new confirmation.

When I contacted Expatrio about the issue, they told me I had to extend the blocked amount and pay a mandatory €69 fee — a charge that would have been unnecessary if they had requested the correct amount in the first place. This feels like a fraudulent and unfair practice.

Complaint 2: They also refused to refund the €69 “Initial Set-up Fee”, even though I activated all required products (bank account and Dr. Walter insurance).

Complaint 3: Expatrio charges €10 for the debit card. You are required to use it once and activate it with a PIN before you can add it to your digital Wallet. However, even after following all the steps, it still can't be added to the Wallet.

Final advice: Think twice before opening your account with Expatrio. Poor compliance, hidden fees, and non-functional services are not what you expect when moving to a new country.

* Forensic Proof Ignored: I have provided a complete, verifiable audit trail. I submitted my Wells Fargo bank statements side-by-side with the Wise transfer receipts. The dates match exactly. The amounts ($3,000 per transaction) match exactly. My name and address are on both documents.

It feels like no one is actually reading the files we upload.
* Gaslighting: They keep telling us to "refund to the student's personal account for simplicity," completely ignoring our repeated explanations that this is not an option for us.

The Bottom Line:
This company operates with a double standard: Zero scrutiny when taking your money, maximum obstruction when returning it.

We are not asking for a favor; we are asking for them to read standard financial documents (Bank Statement + Transfer Receipt) that prove the money came from me.

If you are a parent or sibling funding a student, do not use Expatrio. They will hold your significant capital hostage behind a wall of robotic support emails. We are now facing severe financial strain because they refuse to acknowledge plain evidence.

Complaint 1: The Blocked Amount provided by Expatrio does not comply with the official requirements for the German intensive language course residence permit. The actual legal requirement for 12 months is €13,094 (€1,091.17/month), as confirmed by the Munich Foreigners Office. 

Expatrio only allowed me to deposit €12,133. After transfer fees, the confirmation they issued showed just €11,904 (€992/month), which is below the legal threshold. You can verify this on their own calculator Expatrio's website. 

As a result, the Foreigners Office contacted me, stating the amount was insufficient and requested an additional deposit along with a new confirmation.

When I contacted Expatrio about the issue, they told me I had to extend the blocked amount and pay a mandatory €69 fee — a charge that would have been unnecessary if they had requested the correct amount in the first place. This feels like a fraudulent and unfair practice.

Complaint 2: They also refused to refund the €69 “Initial Set-up Fee”, even though I activated all required products (bank account and Dr. Walter insurance).

Complaint 3: Expatrio charges €10 for the debit card. You are required to use it once and activate it with a PIN before you can add it to your digital Wallet. However, even after following all the steps, it still can't be added to the Wallet.

Final advice: Think twice before opening your account with Expatrio. Poor compliance, hidden fees, and non-functional services are not what you expect when moving to a new country.

I recently went through the interview process for a Senior Product Designer role at Expatrio GmbH, and unfortunately, the experience left a lot to be desired in terms of professionalism, respect, and transparency.

The process started with two initial interviews, which went fairly well. However, I was then assigned a design test task on a Friday, with a deadline to complete it by Monday. The assignment was a full audit and redesign of one of their actual existing products—essentially, a free UX/UI consultation. Despite this extensive workload, I completed the task within the timeframe, expecting feedback and further instructions soon after.

However, after submitting the assignment, I didn’t hear back from Expatrio for nine days. After I followed up, they still didn’t respond for another two days. I reached out again, this time to inform them that I was disconnecting the Figma file due to the complete lack of communication. Only then did I receive a vague response asking me to re-enable access to the file and to “please wait” an additional five days—without any explanation for the delays or silence.

This experience highlighted several red flags for me:

Lack of Respect for Candidates' Time and Effort: Expecting candidates to complete unpaid, real-world product work on such a tight deadline is unprofessional, especially for a senior-level position.
Poor Communication and Transparency: There was no clear timeline or communication about what was happening after each stage, and I was left in the dark for an extended period.
Lack of Process or Professionalism: The vague, “fluffy” responses I received didn’t inspire confidence, and the unstructured nature of the process raised questions about how the company operates internally.

After the long delays and lack of feedback, I decided to withdraw my application. The experience made it clear that this was not an environment that valued transparency or trust—a deal-breaker for me as a senior candidate.

For others considering design roles here, I would strongly advise confirming up front how any design assessments will be used and what the expected timeline is. In the future, I’ll be more careful about agreeing to unpaid work on actual products during interviews, and I’d suggest others do the same.

DETAILED REVIEW:
Where do I start? Expatrio are so good at incorporating scam-like yet legit marketing methods that I can't really help but respect their efforts and skills.
They got me real good with their DeGiS comparisons because they seemed so genuine and accurate.
However, the best comparison I found was that of my own. I used Expatrio and another competitor (check my other review) and after 2 months in Germany, Expatrio seems to be the worse out of the two.

The first issue I had with Expatrio was when I tried to open a blocked account. I had the money and I wanted to do it quickly, but they tried to sell me a payment service called CohortGo as a "faster and cheaper" way to pay. It was anything but. If not having expatrio as a middle man, imagine if that broker himself had another middle man! But they just try to get as much money from you as possible by getting you to use CohortGo.
I fell for CohortGo at first but when it came to actually transferring my money, I emailed them and requested to transfer directly. They reset my account.

While waiting for their reply though, I used the service of another competitor and opened a blocked account with that competitor instead. I'm in Germany now and have had no problems with the competitor's blocked account, even though Expatrio claimed in their DeGiS comparisons that the competitors has problems A, B and C. Quite misleading indeed because none of these problems were true for said competitor based on my experience.

I still however used their TK insurance and they made another mistake and they sent TK a false university start date so I got overcharged for a month (other trustpilot reviews seem to have the same issue!).
I didn't bother to contact Expatrio at this point because a classmate of mine had several issues with Expatrio and advised me to contact TK directly. Cut the middle man!

To conclude, Expatrio is a broker and just like any other broker, you'd think they're provide you with services and products when in fact YOU are the product. They make money from commissions when they bring you, the customer, to a company.

The positives: Expatrio has a quick customer service response and are recognized by the German visa office when applying for a student visa. 

Their business partner in disbursement, Monese unfortunately has literally zero customer service. Monese never answered a single phone call or responded to a single email (I called and emailed several times). I questioned if Monese is a scam service at some point because they have an automated chat but seemingly no human people working for their customer service department. I really question why Expatrio chose them as a partner as it makes everything seem more like an untrustworthy scam to take your funds. I was prepared to get a lawyer to seek legal action against either Monese or Expatrio because it was taking so long to get access to my own funds and no one was updating me on why it was taking so long. I wondered if I just lost a years worth of money to these websites. 

The good news is, you can link your blocked account from Expatrio to a Germany bank and not Monese, which may be easier since most Banks will at least respond to your emails if there is a problem. 

Final Verdict: Expatrio is functional but takes much longer than I expected to get the job done, and is pretty disorganized at getting the job done if you already live in Germany.

Este 2025, con mi marido nos fuimos a Alemania de marzo a julio con la Chancenkarte y FINTIBA era la cuenta bloqueada que más nos recomendaban. Tuvimos el inicio y durante el proceso, muy mala experiencia. Primero, con el envío y recepción del dinero. Nosotros somos de Chile.
Transferimos al rededor de 12.000 euros (que es mucho dinero para nosotros) a finales de diciembre, a una cuenta que Fintiba nos decia que era lo más rápido, con datos bancarios chilenos. Entendiamos que por ser fechas de fiestas, se podría demorar un poco más, pero pasaban las semanas, y no teniamos ninguna confirmación de la recepción del dinero. A todo esto, se supone que el trámite es de máximo 2 semanas, 3 en casos excepcionales. Cada vez que preguntábamos, el mail de ellos era como "les pedimos que tengan paciencia, esto puede demorar, etc." Luego de más de un mes, vuelvo a escribir y me dicen que el dinero no ha llegado y que yo tengo que averiguar con mi banco. Fue terrible ya que estábamos a finales de enero y teníamos comprado el pasaje para marzo, sumado a que los trámites de Consulado son lentos y no avanzan sin el comprobante de la cuenta bloqueada con el dinero.
Luego de hacer las investigaciones pertinentes, donde ellos NO ayudaron, descubrimos que habían 2 intermediarios: uno que recibía el dinero en Chile y lo mandaba a Europa (1), y el otro que lo recibía en Europa (TransferMate) (2) para luego, pasarlo a Fintiba. Sólo escribiéndole a Transfermate que fueron EXCELENTES, pudimos descubrir que el dinero nunca salió de Chile y se quedó estancado más de un mes. No podiamos entender cómo una empresa tan grande como Fintiba, que trabaja con distintos países, no hiciera el seguimiento correspondiente y nos dejara prácticamente solos. Transfermate en 3 dias solucionó todo.
Luego, al llegar a Alemania (porque sí, lo logramos justo a tiempo), empezó otro problema: el primer pago no llegaba, más de un mes así. Ni a mi marido, ni a mi. Y nuevamente, nos decían que nosotros teníamos que averiguar con el banco qué estaba pasando. Abrimos otra cuenta de banco y ahí ya pudimos recibir el pago, el cual vino DOBLE no la primera vez (que se entendería por el atraso), sino los meses posteriores, lo que generaba un desajuste en nuestro orden. Yo entiendo que esto último puede parecer exagerado, pero ya era la gota que rebalsó el vaso.
Realmente fue una muy mala experiencia, esto generó mucho estrés y malestar. Uno entiende que pueden ocurrir contratiempos, especialmente cuando se mezcla dinero y otros países, pero lo que más nos frustraba era la poca claridad y apoyo, pues si bien respondían los correos, estos o eran genéricos o nos decían que nosotros teníamos que resolver por nuestro lado.

From my experience of using blocked account in Fintiba, I can say the following:
1. If you are a student, you are opening a blocked account for the first time, you don't have any specific situations (late arrival, non-standard blocked account term, reunion with a partner), you can be calm - everything worked like clockwork for me and some of my friends. Fast transfer and receipt of funds, quite convenient website and automation of the procedure (checking documents, determining the amount of payments, etc.)

2. If your situation is specific, you should be:
a) Attentive. When renewing your account, keep an eye on the amounts charged. It could be that payments come in earlier than the last month of the period and the next renewal year starts a month earlier. The automation of the system makes it inflexible (it is difficult for specialists to make changes to standard procedures), and correcting past mistakes (additional funds, correcting deadlines) can take valuable time

b) Be prepared for lengthy communication if the issue is not resolved. Response times to support requests (email) can be delayed many times, and it is often necessary to use the phone additionally, to communicate with various specialists, and to find out what exactly the problem is.

From my experience of using blocked account in Fintiba, I can say the following:
1. If you are a student, you are opening a blocked account for the first time, you don't have any specific situations (late arrival, non-standard blocked account term, reunion with a partner), you can be calm - everything worked like clockwork for me and some of my friends. Fast transfer and receipt of funds, quite convenient website and automation of the procedure (checking documents, determining the amount of payments, etc.)

2. If your situation is specific, you should be:
a) Attentive. When renewing your account, keep an eye on the amounts charged. It could be that payments come in earlier than the last month of the period and the next renewal year starts a month earlier. The automation of the system makes it inflexible (it is difficult for specialists to make changes to standard procedures), correcting past mistakes (additional funds, correcting deadlines) can take valuable time

b) Be prepared for lengthy communication if the issue is not resolved. Response times to support requests (email) can be delayed many times, and it is often necessary to use the phone additionally, to communicate with various specialists, and to find out what exactly the problem is.

I can hardly judge the reasons for the difficulties in solving some issues when subscribing to Fintiba, personally I and several of my friends have encountered difficulties in non-standard situations.
Otherwise, I can still recommend Fintiba as a pretty convenient service if you need a blocked account.
